page.layout: One column of running text, with a heading line above it (running head at top); below the text a centred chapter heading "CAPUT IX." followed by an italic summary paragraph in full lines; page number bottom right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: tervi quedam, confusos nonnunquam & permixtos damus, at confictos omnes neutiquam. Quo magis horum temporibus recepta fuit opinio de scriptore Paulo. Sic Haimonis, Remigij, altero & amplius seculo Anselmo vetustiorum, genuinos esse foetus, non diffitentur eruditi. De Ambrosio, Cassiodorus Divin. Lect. C. viii. codicem Epistolarum omnium S. Pauli, reliquisse suavissimâ expositione completum. Si vera Cassiodorus, ergò & Epistolae ad Hebraeos, quando eam in Paulinarum censum, & hic & Ambrosius constantissimè retulêre. Quamvis de hodierni codicis Ambrosiani origine meritò ambigatur.
main_text.head: CAPUT IX.

p.i: Testimonia recentiorum. Qui Paulo tribuunt ex Scholasticis & Pontificijs. Qui ex Lutheranis. Qui ex Reformatis. Magna nomina citata. Qui secùs sentiant. De Calvino. De Confessione Gallicanâ. De Theologis quibusdam aliis. De Novatoribus, Socinianis, Anabaptistis.

page.notes: Running head and heading transcribed from the scan; the page number "I. oᵥ" is a signature-style folio reading ("I. ov" / "I. o5" possibly) and is uncertain. Words in the first line are partly damaged by ink ("tervi quedam" = "tervi-quedam", likely "pervi-quedam" or "servi-quedam"; "nonnunquam" partly obscured). Heading "CAPUT IX." printed in spaced capitals. Doubtful readings: "Qui secùs sentiant" and "Lutheranis" are read with some uncertainty; "Lutheranis" is printed "Lætheranis"/"Lutheranis" with damaged letters. The first line also contains a broken word at the top ("tervi quedam" beginning cut off by ink smear), so it is marked as a continuation fragment.
